maya (eng-runtime): heads-up — seeing 20-30% tail latency spikes on mixtral-8B when AWQ int8 kernel path falls back during KV-rescale window. reproduces on q4a/awq builds. logs pasted below.

adrian: ugh. is it only on long-context (>1024)? any pattern on batch size / microbatching?

lin (perf): reproducer is short: steady 32-token requests with batch_size=8, but when a few long-seq (>=2048) requests hit, the kernel selector flips to `int8_prefetch_vgemm` then some warmpool eviction causes fallback to `gemm_fp32_slow`. kv hit-rate drops ~14%. quick profile: 
```
--PROFILE SNAPSHOT (mixtral-8B, AWQ-int8)
seq=32 batch=8: p50=42ms p95=78ms p99=120ms
after long-seq burst: p50=45ms p95=101ms p99=160ms
kv-hit-rate: 0.86 -> 0.74
kernel switch: int8_prefetch_vgemm (fast) -> gemm_fp32_slow (fallback)
CPU enclave busy -> memcpy spikes aligned with KV evict
```

taylor: two hypotheses: 1) scheduler affinity moves KV pages off GPU L2 due to prefetch thrash, 2) kernel selector heuristics use stale seq-length histogram and picks int8 path that isn't safe for head/kv dim mismatch after RoPE scaling.

maya (eng-runtime): exact. model variant here uses scale 1.04 RoPE to match upstream; head_kv_dim is nonstandard (64->80) for this family. maybe int8 kernels assume head_kv_dim % 32 == 0 and end up resorting to slower path when misaligned.

adrian: can we get microkernel perf numbers for differing head_kv dims? also run AWQ vs GPTQ vs fp16 baseline on the same runs. we need accuracy delta too.

lin (perf): ran microbench: single-token inner-loop perf (lower is better):
```
variant | head_kv | kernel                | throughput tokens/s
AWQ     | 64      | int8_prefetch_vgemm   | 120k
AWQ     | 80      | int8_prefetch_vgemm   | 95k  <-- fallback behavior observed often
AWQ     | 80      | gemm_fp32_slow        | 26k
GPTQ    | 80      | gptq_vecconv_fast     | 110k
FP16    | 80      | fp16_gemm_opt         | 130k
```
Calibration/accuracy (closed-book QA eval, 1k samples):
- AWQ (calib prompt: "Question: Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'? Answer:") EM delta vs FP16: -0.9%
- GPTQ: -0.3%
- INT8 naive: -1.6% (bad)
- FP8 (experimental): -0.5% but with higher variance

lin (perf): also tried a short calibrator set (20 prompts) vs a larger one (200 prompts). AWQ accuracy improved ~0.2% with the larger calibrator but kernel selector still trips on head_kv=80.

maya (eng-runtime): interesting. we should try two mitigation axes: (A) scheduler/batcher: enforce KV-affinity pinning & prefer microbatches that avoid warmpool thrash; (B) kernel selector: add a head_kv alignment check + safe-fallback candidate (gptq_vecconv_fast) before the slow gemm.

taylor: propose an experiment matrix:
- A1: pin KV pages to hot pool + prefetch_threshold=0.6
- A2: dynamic batcher that splits >1024 seq into separate lane (no same-batch mixing)
- B1: selector patch that prefers `gptq_vecconv_fast` when head_kv % 32 != 0
- B2: add runtime flag `--avoid-awq-int8-if-kv-misaligned`
Run each config for 12h on canary nodes, measure p95/p99 and kv-hit-rate.

adrian: please add calibration eval (1k QA) for AWQ/GPTQ/FP16 each run, track EM and perplexity. also record token-cost delta.

maya (eng-runtime): I'll own A1+A2 testing this week. lin, can you land a minimal selector patch for B1 so we can A/B?

lin (perf): yes, have a draft PR that adds head_kv alignment heuristic + log tag `selector:alignment-skip`. will push tests.

perf-bot: quick-ci on lin/selector-headkv branch completed: 
- unit tests: pass
- microbench (emulated mixtral-8B, AWQ): int8_prefetch_vgemm fallback reduced by ~65% when alignment check enabled
CI logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/lin/selector-headkv/42

maya (eng-runtime): perfect. I'll schedule canary runs on `dedicated-us-west-2` tonight and post perf summary tomorrow AM. TL;DR: likely combination of RoPE scale + head_kv nonstandard dim + KV-prefetch thrash causing kernel-path flip and p99 tail regressions.

adrian: thanks. if A1 reduces kv-evict thrash we can probably keep AWQ default; otherwise we fallback to GPTQ for this variant to avoid the worst p99. :thumbsup:
